ORAL ANSWERS TO QUESTIONS 
Closure of Loss Making NTC Mills 
*201. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA : 
SHRIMATI BIMBA RAIKAR: 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased to state: 
(a) Whether Government have decided to close down 22 loss making 
National Textile Corporation (NTC) mills in Maharashtra; 
(b) if so, how money will be arranged to pay the workers compensation, 
VRS and other terminal benefits; and 
(c) the scheme chalked out for other NTC mills in India? 
THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (S HRI SHANKERSINH VAGHELA): 
(a) to (c) A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) As per the Rehabilitation Schemes approved by BIFR for NTC (South 
Maharashtra) and NTC (Maharashtra North), 18 loss-making mills out of a 
total of 35 mills in the State of Maharashtra have been closed. The remaining 
17 mills are slated for revival under the scheme. 
 (b) NTC has mobilised Rs. 644 Cr by floating Government Guaranteed 
Bonds for paying VRS compensation and other terminal benefits to the 
14,500 employees who opted for VRS in Maharashtra. 
(c) Rehabilitation Schemes have been approved by Government/BIFR for 
reviving 53 mills and to close down 66 unviable mills of NTC after giving 
VRS benefits to the affected employees.

*202. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the Mi nister of TEXTILES be pleased te-
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that he had made a statement that our exports will 
double in the next two years quelling fears that cheaper Chinese products 
will, hit the Indian industry; 
(b) how far we will benefit from the free global trade in the textile market; 
and 
(c) what is our action plan to put thrust on making the "Made in India" 
brand popular in the world market? 
THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI SHANKERSINH VAGHELA): 
(a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) and (b) Yes, Sir. There is a general perception that India's textile 
exports would increase in the post quota regime starting from 1 st January 
2004. According to a recent study by CRISIL (commissioned by Indian 
Cotton Mills Federation), the India's textile and clothing industry has the 
potential to double the country's share of the global textiles and clothing 
market to 6 per cent, implying export earnings of US$ 40 billion by 2010. 
The free global trading regime would result in increased international 
trade in textiles thus providing greater export opportunities for the indigenous 
textile industry. At the same time, it will expose the domestic 
6 

[15 December, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
industry to increased competition in the international market. The industry 
will have to improve its efficiency and productivity to meet the emerging 
global competition. 
(c) Government is already operating a Brand Equity Fund Scheme to 
promote Indian brands in overseas market with the primary objective of 
brand promotion. The scheme is also making the "Made in India" label a 
symbol of quality, competitive price, reliability and service to the customer. 
The Central assistance under the scheme is provided for the following 
activities: 
*To finance the activities linked to the objective of brand promotion as 
distinct from export promotion. 
*Undertake international promotions to project India as a whole as well as 
specific production sectors viz., Industry, agriculture, services etc. 
*Support sectoral promotions: e.g., within industry, specific industries like 
engineering, textiles, electronics, pharmaceuticals, softwares etc. 
*Support product group promotion within each  sector: e.g., within 
engineering products, segments like cycles, automobiles etc. 
*Support particular brands which have achieved world class quality and 
performance standards. 
*Support domestic awareness generation programme directed at quality 
and high business ethics. 
The scheme is also applicable to pr omotion of India's apparel and textile 
brand in the markets abroad. 
In addition, the Export Promotion Councils have been undertaking export 
promotion events like participation in overseas exhibitions/fairs, organizing 
BSMs abroad, overseas publicity, sp onsoring trade delegations etc. in 
consultation with Indian Missions abroad to improve the brand image of 
Indian Textiles.

road to Leh.

both the North and South portals of the proposed tunnel at Rohtang at a cost 
of Rs. 30 crore. Two access roads were to be constructed of 2.7 kms (North 
Portal) and access road to the South port al of 23.8 kms. The access road to 
the North portal of the tunnel has almost been completed and 23.46 kms. of

Tunnei and other related works is Rs. 1709.35 crore. The work relating to

Statement 
Report of the Task Force: 
8. RECOMMENDATIONS OF TH E TASK FORCE WITH RESPECT 
TO LONG-TERM ARRANGEMENTS. 
8.1 The two State PSUs, KELTEC/KELTRON, are valued suppliers to 
Defence Establishments and Space De partment for over a decade. The 
companies have been more involved in supplies of developmental nature, 
which does not provide a long-term and planned feed for their consistent 
growth and upgradation. It is desirable to provide the Companies with a 
consistent and committed workload through long-term procurement 
relationship. 
8.2 HAL, BEL, BDL, OFB, ISRO and DRDO have identified items for 
such long-term relationship. These are listed in Chapter 7.0. DRDO and 
ISRO have already a successful ongoing procedure for placing orders on 
these firms. Continuation and further enlargement of this relationship would 
be useful for mutual benefit of these organisations. However, with respect to 
DPSUs and OFB a viable procedure for implementation of such a relationship 
be looked into and approved by compet ent authority because at present they 
are bound to follow the general tendering procedure based on 
Government/CVC guidelines. 
8.3 For orders of development nature, small batch size and requiring 
constant interaction and upgradation of  skills and facilities appropriate long 
term relationship with KELTEC and KELTRON would be desirable.' 
8.4 The Task Force, after considerable deliberations, recommends the 
following:— 
 
8.4.1 The DPSUs, DRDO, OFs, etc.  may appoint KELTEC and 
KELTRON as a 'Preferred Vendor' as currently being done by Space 
Department, in specified areas of procurement. The buying company may 
follow the limited tender process within the preferred vendors for such 
procurements. 
8.4.2 In view of the financial constraints of KELTEC and KELTRON, 
the long-term orders may include advance payment/free issue of material 
along wtih orders, wherever possible. 
36 

[15 December, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
8.4.3 DPSUs/OFB may also consider investment in upgradation of 
specific technologies as needed for their niche production coupled with 
operational control, if desired. 
8.4.4 The items and work identified may be put on a 'Rate Contract' for a 
period ranging from one to five years, depending on the nature of items, 
volumes involved and the spread over a time frame. The 'Rates' and terms 
shall be mutually agreed by th e buying company and KELTEC/KELTRON. 
For the period when this Rate Contract  is in vogue, th e buying company can 
straightaway procure from KELTEC and KELTRON based on agreed 
schedule, without having to follow any tendering process. Arrangement 
currently in practice with DGS&D in this respect may be considered. 
8.5 OFB representative has cited synergy between OFB and KELTEC and 
some of the units of KELTRON and has indicated an option to acquire 
KELTEC and some units of KELTRON e ither as subsidiary or direct 
integration with OFB. 
Considering the proposal from Kerala Government to the Central 
Government for acquiring KELTEC and KELTRON the Government may 
examine this in details including due diligence.

Firing by Sri Lankan Navy on Indian Fishermen 
1306. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN: W ill the Minister of DEFENCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Sri Lankan Navy is patrolling the waters 
around Kachatheevu Island, indulging in firing at our fishermen, against the 
Kachatheevu agreement; 
(b) the steps taken by the Indian Navy to protect Indian fishermen; and 
(c) will Government press our Navy to patrol around Kachatheevu to 
safeguard the lives and boats of our fishermen? 
THE MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE): (a) to 
(c) The Kachatheevu Island located in the Palk Bay was handed over to Sri 
Lanka by India in 1974, through an Indo-Sri Lanka agreement. This 
44 

[15 December, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
island therefore lies in Sri Lankan wate rs. Sri Lankan Naval Vessels patrol 
the Sri Lanka waters aroun d Kachatheevu Island. It has also been alleged by 
Indian fishermen that Sri Lankan Navy resort to firing. 
The Indian Navy/Coast Guard and Sri Lankan Navy regularly undertake 
coordinated patrolling in the Palk Bay, within their respective and agreed 
waters of the International Maritime Boundary Line (IMBL). This 
coordinated patrolling includes areas near Kachatheevu Island also. The 
effectiveness of such patrolling is regularly reviewed through meetings 
between Indian Navy/Coast Guard and Sri Lankan Navy. During such review 
meetings, it is also emphasized by the Indian side, that Indian fishermen 
apprehended by the Sri Lankan Navy should not be harmed. 
Further, to educate the Indian fishermen, community interaction 
programmes are also undertaken by th e Coast Guard to advise the Indian 
fishermen community not to cross the International Maritime Boundary Line 
into Sri Lankan waters, for fishing purposes. These community interaction 
programmes emphasize that such poaching is an international offence 
making the fishermen liable to be apprehended by the Sri Lankan Navy.

2. The following schemes for the welfare, rehabilitation and resettlement 
of ex-servicemen are being implemented:- 
I. REHABILITATION AND RESETTLEMENT SCHEMES:— 
(A) Re-employment: 
(i) Reservations in jobs:- The Central and State Governments are 
providing a number of concessions to ex-servicemen for their re-employment 
in Central/State Government posts. These include reservation of posts/ 
relaxation in age and educational qualifications, exemption from payment of 
application/examination fees, priority employment to disabled ex-
servicemen. The Central Government has reserved 10% of vacancies in 
Group C posts and 20% in Group D posts for ex-servicemen. Central Public 
Sector Undertakings and Nationalised Banks provide 14.5% reservation in 
Group C and 24.5% in Group D posts available with them. 10% posts of 
Assistant Commandants in Central Para Military Forces are also reserved for 
ex-servicemen. 100% posts are reserv ed for ex-servicemen in Defence 
Security Corps. In addition, many State Governments are providing 
reservation to ex-servicemen in the State Government jobs. 
During the year 2003, 11659 ex-ser vicemen have been provided re-
employment. 
(ii) Security Agencies:- The Directorate General of Resettlement 
registers/sponsors security agencies for providing security guards to various 
Public Sector Undertakings and indust ries in private sector. The Scheme, 
besides offering employment opportunities to ex-servicemen, also provides 
self-employment to retired defence officers. During the year 2004 (up to 
November), 18,261 ex-servicemen have been provided re-employment under 
the scheme. 
59

(B) Self-employment: 
(i) Loan Assistance Schemes:- Government has formulated several 
schemes for encouraging and giving financial support by way of loans to ex-
servicemen entrepreneurs intending to set up small and medium industries. 
Important self employment schemes are Self Employment for Ex-Servicemen 
II (SEMFEX-II), National Equity Fund (NEF) Scheme and SEMFEX-III. 
Applications for sanction of loans are submitted by ex-servicemen directly to 
the concerned Zila Sainik Boards in the States. Applications are scrutinised 
and those who satisfy eligibility criteria and other terms and conditions are 
recommended for sanction of loan through banks and financial institutions. 
Number of ex-servicemen/widows benefited from the above schemes is as 
under: 
SEMFEX-II        16,843      (Since inception of the scheme in 1988-89)

NEF 36 (Since inception of the scheme in 2000-01) 
(ii) Ex-Servicemen Coal Transportation Scheme: 
Directorate General Resettlement sponsors Ex-Servicemen Coal Transport 
Companies for the execution of loading and transportation of coal in various 
coal subsidiaries of Coal India Lim ited. The unemployed retired officers 
registered with Directorate General Resettlement are selected to form Ex-
Servicemen Coal Transpor t Companies and are sponsored to respective coal 
subsidiaries for five years, extendable  by another four years. Presently, 101 
such companies are operating under the various coal subsidiaries of Coal 
India Limited. 
(iii) Coal Tipper Scheme: 
Widows of defence personnel who died while in service due to causes 
attributable to military service can be sponsored by DGR for attaching one 
tipper truck in their name with an Ex-Servicemen Coal Transport Company. 
The eligible widows have to deposit Rs. 85,000/-with any one of the 
nominated companies towards margin m oney, loan processing, insurance, 
road tax etc. for the tipper to be acq uired. The coal transport company is 
responsible for processing, running and maintenance costs of the tipper. The 
widow is paid Rs. 3,000/- per month for five years and thereafter, the initial 
deposit amount of Rs. 85,000/- is repaid to the

widow. At present, 289 widows/disabled soldiers are availing the benefit of

Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas have reserved eight percent of the 
Oil Product Agencies, i.e. LPG dealership, petrol pumps, kerosene 
distributorship etc. in the marketing plan for widows and dependents of those 
who died in war/peace with death attributable to military service and disabled 
soldiers with disability of 20 percent and above attributable to military 
service. 753 eligibility certificates have been issued under Defence Category 
by Directorate General Resettlement during 2004 upto November, 2004. 
(v) Management of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Stations in National 
Capital Region (NCR):

Gas Ltd. was launched as a pilot project in July 2001. The scheme has been 
extended to retired officers. As on date, 73 ex-servicem en are managing

Ex-Servicemen/widows of Defence personnel who died while in service 
are eligible to apply for allotment of Army surplus/phased out vehicles. Ex-
servicemen can apply to Zila/Rajya Sainik Boards for registration and 
onward transmission to Army Headquarters for allotment on the basis of 
depot wise seniority maintained by them. During the year 2004, 452 surplus 
vehicles have been allotted to ex-servicemen up to November, 2004. 
(vii) Allotment of Mother Dairy Milk and Fruit & Vegetable Shops in and 
around Delhi: 
Junior Commissioned Officers/Other Ranks are allotted Mother Diary 
Milk Shops and Fruit & Vegetable shops in National Capital Region. During 
the year 2004,1735 ex-s ervicemen have been provided placement by 
allotment of Mother Diary Booths and Fruit & Vegetable shops till date.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI MANIKRAO GAVIT): (a) No, Sir. The Chief Registrars of Birth and

(b) and (c) Yes, Sir; The Government have set the goal of achieving

Government have initiated various steps which inter-alia include regular 
monitoring of the levels of registration, providing assistance to the states for

(d) The imbalance in child sex ratio is chiefly due to preference for a son 
resulting in female foeticide and continued neglect of girl child leading to 
higher mortality among them. In order to contain the practice of female 
foeticide, the Pre-natal Diagnostic Te chniques (Regulation and Preventions 
of Misuse) Act, 1994 was put into effect from 1.1.1996. The Act has been 
amended since then and made more stringent. The responsibility of the 
implementation of the Act is with the States/UTs administration. 
To bring about a change in the attitude towards girl child and to overcome 
general social prejudice against them , the Government of India has been 
advertising through the radio, televisi on and print media to create awareness 
against the practice of pre-natal determination of sex and female foeticide. 
Workshop and seminars are being organized through voluntary organizations 
at the State and sub-state levels for the same purpose. Help and cooperation 
has been sought from religious leaders as well as medical fraternity to curb 
this practice. In addition the Government has been implementing the scheme 
of "Balika Samriddhi Yojna" since 19 97 with multi-purpose objectives of 
changing the negative family and community attitude towards the girl child,

Delhi High Court's Guidelines for Delhi Police 
1371. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Delhi High Court has laid down guidelines for 
police and has asked for their strict implementation to ensure impartial probe 
in cases of murder, rape etc.; 
(b) if so, the details of these guidelines; and 
(c) what is the action plan of Government  to ensure that these are strictly 
adhered to by all concerned to control manipulations and padding in criminal 
cases? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI S. REGUPATHY): (a) and (b) The High Court of Delhi vide their 
order dated 2nd November, 2004 in Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 1242/2003 
titled Mahender Singh Chhabra Vs. State of N.C.T. of Delhi and others had, 
inter alia, issued the following directions: 
In all the complaints/FIRs for the commission of offences of murder under 
Section 302 IPC, culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 
304 IPC, death of a woman under suspicious circumstances within seven 
years of marriage under Section 304-B IPC, offence of rape under Section 
376 IPC, and dacoity with murder punishable under Section 396 IPC, the 
following guidelines shall be followed: 
(i) Upon receipt of a complaint or re gistration of FIR for any of the afore-
said offences, immediate steps shall be taken to associate a scientist from 
Forensic Science Laboratory or some other laboratory or department in the 
investigations. The Investigating Officer shall conduct investigations on the 
points suggested by him also under his guidance and advice. 
(ii) To ensure that the complainant or victim of crime does not remain in 
dark about the investigations regarding his complaint/FIR, the complainant or 
victim shall be kept informed about the progress of investigations. In case the 
complainant gives anything in writing and requests the Investigating Officer 
for investigations on any particular aspect of the matter, the same shall be 
adverted to by the Investigating Officer . Proper entries shall be made by 
Investigating Officer in case diaries in regard to the steps taken on the basis 
of the request made by the complainant. The complainant, 
102 

[15 December, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
however, shall not be entitled to know the confidential matters, if any, the 
disclosure of which may jeopardize the investigations. 
(iii) Whenever the Sub Divisional Magi strate/Magistrate is requested to 
record a dying declaration, video recording also shall be done with a view to 
obviate subsequent objections to the genuineness of the dying declaration. 
(iv) The investigations for the aforesaid offences shall be personally 
supervised by the Assistant Commi ssioner of Police of the area. The 
concerned Deputy Commissioner of Police shall also undertake fornightly 
review thereof. 
(v) The material prosecution witnesses cited in any of the aforesaid 
offences shall be ensured safety and protection by the Station House Officer 
concerned, who shall personally attend to their complaints, if any. 
(vi) Orientation be given to the Doctors, who prepare Medico Legal 
Certificates or conduct post mortem s to ensure that the Medico Legal 
Certificates as well as post mortem reports are up to the mark and stand 
judicial scrutiny in Courts. 
The High Court of Delhi in the aforesaid orders further directed the 
Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi and the Delhi Police 
(respondents No. 1 and 2) to ensure that the aforesaid directions are 
immediately enforced and followed by all concerned. 
(c) Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi and Delhi Police is 
being advised to issue necessary instructions for implementation of these 
guidelines.

Illegal Bangladeshis in Delhi 
1374. SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY:  Will the Minister of HOME 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have been directed by the Delhi 
High Court to conduct survey of illegal Bangladeshi migrants in the capital 
city of Delhi; and 
115 

RAJYA SABHA [15 December, 2004] 
(b) if so, whether Government have started the survey to identify the 
illegal Bangladeshi migrants? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI S. REGUPATHY): (a) The High Court of Delhi vide their order dated 
22nd September, 2004 in Writ Petition (c) No. 3170/2001 and Writ Petition 
(c) No. 2925/1999 directed the Government of NCT of Delhi to undertake the 
survey to detect illegal Bangladeshi migrants residing in Delhi and to deport 
them immediately. 
(b) In pursuance of the aforesaid directions, the Government of National 
Capital Territory of Delhi has asked the Delhi Police to set up more task force 
teams, in addition to the 10 existing teams to speed up the work of detection 
and deportation. It has also directed the Commissioner of Food and Civil 
Supplies in the Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi to extend 
co-operation to the task force teams by deputing Supply Inspectors to 
participate in these teams. Accordingly, Delhi Police has constituted six 
additional task force teams raising the total number of teams to 16 to speed up 
the work of detection and deportation of illegal Bangladeshi migrants. 
Overhauling of Police Investigation Procedure 
1375. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government propose to launch an ambitious 
crime intelligence and overhaul police investigation procedure across the 
country; 
(b) if so, the details of the project; and 
(c) how far this would help to control crimes, harassment to women and 
usher in welfare of the general public? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI MANIKRAO GAVIT): (a) to (c) A Pilot Project has been sanctioned 
in the State of Haryana, Punjab, Ja mmu & Kashmir, Uttar Pradesh, West 
Bengal, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka and NCT of Delhi for introducing an 
Organized Crime Intelligence System (OCIS). 
116 

[15 December, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
The information collected under OCIS  from the State Organized Crime 
Units will be available at the central database at NCRB for sharing among 
various States and law enforcement agencies. Criminal Intelligence thus 
available will enable the States to undertake pro-active policing to prevent 
crimes including crimes against women. Such information is also expected to 
assist Law Enforcement Agencies in the effective and speedy investigation of 
crimes, thereby helping in controlling crimes and enhance public safety. 
Need to Institutionalize the meetings of Inter-State Council 
1376. SHRI NILOTPAL BASU:: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that there are several pending issues which are to be 
taken up in the Inter-State Council; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) whether Government are planning to institutionalize the meetings of 
the Council on any regular basis, if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI MANIKRAO GAVIT): (a) and (b) The Inter-State Council is a 
recommendatory body which may investigate, discuss and make 
recommendations on subjects, in which some or all the States or the Union 
and one or more of the States have a common interest, as maybe brought up 
before it. The Ministries of the Union Government or the State Governments 
may refer the issues to the Secretariat of the Inter-State Council for placing 
before the Council. The Inter-State Council has also adopted guidelines for 
identifying and selecting issues to be brought up before it. The Inter-State 
Council has primarily been considering, the recommendations of the Sakaria 
Commission on Centre-State relations. In its eight meetings held so far, the 
Council has completed deliberations on  all of the 247 recommendations of 
the Sakaria Commission. 
(c) The Presidential order dated 28 May,  1990 establishing the Inter-State 
Council already provides that the Counc il should meet at least thrice every 
year and at such time and place as the Chairman may appoint in this behalf.

1383. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: W ill the Minister of POWER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that floods have affected the production of power at 
the Nathpa Jhakri Power Plant in Himachal Pradesh; 
(b) if so, the details thereof with areas  denied power due to stoppage of 
power production in the plant; 
(c) the reasons why adequate steps were not taken to protect the plant in 
the wake of flood situation; and

THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P.M. SAYEED): (a) No, Sir. 
However, the threat of an unprecedented flood affected the production of 
power at Nathpa Jhakri Power Plant in Himachal Pradesh. 
(b) During August, 2004, a massive  landslide has created a 'dam' and 
blocked the river Pareechu, a tributary to Spiti/Satluj River in Tibet in China 
and formed an artificial lake. Bursting of  this 'dam' could cause a flash flood 
in Satluj Valley. As a precautionary meas ure, a red alert for the safety of the 
people and the Project was declared by Government of India and 
Government of Himachal Pradesh. Generation was stopped for about ten 
days due to possibility of flash floods and high content of silt in the river 
waters. Approximately 491 MU of generation was lost. Power from Nathpa 
Jhakri Project is supplied to northern grid comprising the States of Jammu & 
Kashmir, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan,  Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, 
Chandigarh and Delhi which were denied their share of power from Nathpa 
Jhakri Hydro Electric Project during this period. 
123 

RAJYA SABHA       [15 December, 2004] 
(c) Adequate steps were taken to protect the plant in the wake of the flood 
alert situation. All the 5 radial gates on the dam were kept open and the 
pondage of the dam was kept to its natural flow. Water level in the dam 
pondage area was kept at lowest level of EL 1462 for absorbing heavy flood. 
All the Intake Gates of the 27.4 km long Head Race Tunnel were closed. All 
the six Draft Tube Gates were closed, all the gates at Tail Race Tunnel out 
fall were closed and all the six machines were shutdown. 
(d) After ascertaining the factual positi on of the artificial lake on river 
Pareechu from various sources, the power production was re-started with 
effect from 17.08.2004 and gradually raised to the optimum level.

Criteria for demarcating poverty line 
1403. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister of 
RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the criteria for declaring poor in Indian official poverty line is 
lowest after China in the world; 
(b) if so, what is the criteria for earmarking poverty line; and 
(c) the action proposed to take care of basic needs of India's poor as is 
being done by China? 
THE MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI RAGHUVANSH 
PRASAD SINGH): (a) The poverty line of countries can not usually be 
compared since the factors taken into account to determine the poverty line 
may be different for different countries. 
(b) The poverty line in India is expressed in terms of per capita 
consumption expenditure needed to attain a minimum amount of calorie 
intake of food consumption along  with a minimum amount of non-food 
expenditure in order to meet the requirements of clothing, shelter, transport 
etc. The per capita consumption norm has been fixed at Rs. 49.09 per 
month in rural areas and Rs. 56.64 per month in urban areas at 1973-74 
prices at national level corresponding to a basket of goods and services, 
anchored on a norm of per capita daily calorie requirement of 2400 kcal. In 
rural area and 2400 kcal. in urban ar eas. The state-specific poverty line 
are derived from the national level poverty line, using State specific price 
indices and inter-state price differentials. The national poverty line at 1999- 
2000 prices is Rs. 327.56 per month in rural areas and Rs. 454.11 per 
capita per month in urban areas. 
(c) The Government has adopted a three pronged strategy for reducing 
poverty (i) acceleration of economic growth with a focus on sectors which 
are employment intensive (ii) human and social development through 
provision of basic minimum services and (iii) targeted anti poverty 
programmes. 
In order to take care of basic needs of India's poor at the village level, an 
initiative in the form of Prime Minister's Gramodaya Yojana (PMGY) was 
launched. The PMGY envisages Additional Central Assistance for selected 
basic minimum services in order to focus on certain priority areas of the 
142 

[15 December, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
Government. These include primary health, primary education, rural shelter, 
drinking water, rural electrification and nutrition. 
The Ministry of Rural Development also implements through the State 
Governments, the major schemes of the Sampoorna Gramin Rozgar Yojana 
(SGRY) and the Swarnjayanti Gram Sw arozgar Yojana (SGSY) to provide 
wage and self employment to members of the rural families living below the 
poverty line in all the rural areas of the country. Other schemes of the 
Ministry of Rural Development such as the Prime Ministers Gram Sadak 
Yojana (PMGSY), the Indira Awaas Yojana (IAY) and the Watershed 
Development Programme are also designed to improve the living conditions 
in the rural areas as well as indirec tly provide employment. Government has 
also recently launched a National Food for work Programme in 150 most 
backward Districts in the country with  the objective to provide additional 
employment opportunities to the rural poor. 
In addition, with effect from June, 1997 the Public Distribution system in 
India was streamlined by issuing special cards to families Below Poverty 
Line (BPL) and selling food grains under PDS to them specially subsidized 
prices which was about 50% of the ec onomic costs. Under the new scheme 
viz. the Targeted Public Distribution Sy stem (TPDS) each poor family is 
entitled to 35kgs. of foodgrains.

Victory in European Patent Office over Hessian 
1414. SHRI KARNENDU  BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of 
TEXTILES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have won the first major battle 
before European Patent Office over Hessian (a variety of jute cloth used for 
packing and as land cover) which will prove to be a much needed reprive for 
the jute sector: 
(b) if so, whether it will have any impact on reduction of dumping duty 
on import of jute bags from Indian; and 
(c) to what extent? 
THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI SHANKERSINH VAGHELA): 
(a) Yes, sir. India won the European Patent Case on Waste Treatment using 
Hessian. Govt, of India through JMDC pleaded for revocation of the 
impugned patent and refuted the arguments of the patentee by substantiating 
the similarity of Hessian with Geo-textiles. JMDC also argued that the patent 
is against the "Order Pub lic" because, if allowed, it would tend to block free 
trade and business of Hessian in European market covering 14 countries and 
would lead to imposition of undue royalty  and license fee on the public. The 
Appeal Board rejected the patent on th e ground of "lack of inventive steps" 
on 6th May, 2004. 
(b) and (c) There is no anti-dumping duty on import of Indian Jute Goods 
in any of the European countries. Furt her, there is no co-relation between the 
patent case and dumping duty on import of Indian Jute g oods. There will, 
therefore, be no impact on dumping duty on Import of Jute goods from India 
by virtue of winning the European patent battle.

Schemes for providing basic sports facilities 
†1425. SHRI PYARELAL KHAND ELWAL: Will the Minister of 
YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) the scheme formulated by Government for providing basic facilities' for 
the development of sports in the country; 
(b) the State-wise details of funds provided to various States under the said 
scheme; 
(c) the funds allocated to Madhya Pradesh for construction of stadium 
during last three years and the number of pending proposals, the details 
thereof; and 
(d) the reasons for delay in sanctioning the proposals sent by Madhya 
Pradesh for organizing activities for youths? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI SUNIL 
DUTT): (a) Central assistance in accord ance with the approved pattern is 
provided to State Governments, Institutio ns etc. for creation cf basic sports 
facilities for the development of sports in the country, under the following 
schemes: 
(i) Grants for Creation of Sports Infrastructure; 
(ii) Grants to Rural Schools for purchase of sports equipment and 
development of playground; 
(iii) Grants for Promotion of Sports in Universities & Colleges; and 
(iv) Grants for Installation of Synthetic Playing Surfaces. 
(b) The State-wise details of funds provided under the above mentioned 
schemes during the last 3 years (2001-02 to 2003-04) and current year 
2004-05 (as on 30.11.2004) have been indicated in the enclosed statement. 
(See below) 
(c) State-wise allocation is not made under the above mentioned 
schemes. Grants are provided subject to the receipt of viable proposals 
from the State Government. The details  of Central assistance released to 
Madhya Pradesh for construction of stadia under the Scheme of "Grants

and train a minimum of 100 students from every State;

potential for continuous training and sponsorship by Government;

sports training with a view on the next two Olympics', and 
(d) the other steps proposed to plan for the next two Olympics? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI SUNIL 
DUTT): (a) to (d) No, Sir. However, the Government of India, through its 
various schemes, augments the efforts of the State Government in promotion 
of sports all over the country. 
At present Sports Authority of India (SAI) is implementing the following 
schemes for promotion and development of sports in the country:— 
National Sports Talent Contest (NSTC) Army 
Boys Sports Company (ABSC) Special Area 
Games (SAG) SAI Training Centre (STC) 
Centre of Excellence (COX)

Under ABSC, ten additional centres have been identified during this 
financial year. 
The induction of talented trainees in the above-mentioned schemes is a 
regular feature and out of these talented  youngsters those who show potential 
are included for the national camps/participation in international competitions 
including the Olympics. 
Planning and preparation for events like Olympics, Asian Games and 
Commonwealth Games is an ongoing process. Action plans for above games 
are prepared in consultation with the concerned National Sports Federations, 
National Coaches, Eminent sportspersons and Experts. 
Expansion of Youth Activities at University and School Level 
1431. SHRI SiM. LALJAN BASHA:  Will the Minister of YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government has not formulated any 
imaginative schemes for youth in the country; 
(b) if so, whether there is any proposal to expand youth activities at the 
university and school level; 
(c) whether any effort will be made to involve the private sector in 
development of sports infrastructure and games for the youth of the country; 
and 
(d) if so, the details thereof ? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI SUNIL 
DUTT): (a) and (b) Apart from the regular schemes of the Ministry, a new 
scheme for the Development and Empowerment of Adolescents focussing on 
the age group 10-19 years has been launched. Presently, National Service 
Scheme (NSS) is implemented through Universities/Colleges and Senior 
Secondary level (+ 2 Councils) in the country. The scheme is proposed to be 
expanded further. 
(c) and (d) The government has adopted the scheme of State Sports 
Academy during the Tenth Plan period. The scheme envisages setting up of 
an Academy at the approximate cost of Rs. 9.68 crore by the Central 
government, State government/UT administration and a sponsor as a joint

venture in the ratio of 25:24:51. It is envisaged that the Academy would be

sports infrastructure. 
Sports Authority of India has entered with an Memorandum of 
Understanding (MoU) with Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and 
Industry (FICCI) and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) has entered into an 
MoU with Confederation of Indian Industry (CM) for cooperation in the field 
of sports. 
Government has also taken initiatives for encouraging contribution from 
the public and the private sector under its scheme of National Sports 
Development Fund (NSDF).

1432. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:  Will the Minister of YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that high cost of equipments and sports tools is 
acting as an impediment to sports development in the country; 
(b) if so, whether Government propose to subsidise sports equipments like 
archery and shooting equipments and gymnastics for schools and colleges 
and to provide sports equipments and tools of games to schools and colleges 
at cheaper rates; 
(c) the details of plan of Government to make sports and games more 
accessible to talented youth in the country; and 
(d) the status of such efforts by SAI and other agencies dealing with 
sports? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI SUNIL 
DUTT): (a) to (b) The cost of equipments and sports tools varies from sport 
to sport. However, the state governments/schools/colleges can avail 
assistance for purchase of various sports equipments under the schemes of 
"Grants to Rural Schools for purchase of sports equipment and development 
of playfield" and "Grants for Promotion of Sports in Universities & 
Colleges". Under the Rural schools Scheme, 100% central assistacne upto a 
maximum limit of Rs. 1.00 lakh for non-consumables and Rs. 25,000/- 
195 

RAJYA SABHA [15 December, 2004] 
for consumable sports equipments is provided to the schools situated in rural 
areas without any matching share. In  the case of Universities/Colleges, 
central assistance upto a maximum limit of Rs. 3.00 lakh is provided for 
purchase of non-consumable sports equipments without any matching share. 
The approval of central assistance under the above scheme is, however, 
subject to the receipt of viable prop osals from the institutions in accordance 
with the approved norms of the schemes. 
(c) and (d) "Sports' being a state subject, promotion of the same at the. 
State level is the responsibility of the state governments. The Ministry also 
grants assistance to National Sports Federations for holding National 
Championship at sub-junior, junior and senior level in both men as well as 
women categories. 
The Ministry operates the Rural Sports Programme with a view to broad 
basing games and sports and tapping hidden talent in rural areas. The scheme 
has two sub components-organisation of rural sports tournaments and the 
North East Sports Festival. 
Synthetic Athletic Track and hockey su rfaces are exempted from custom 
duty under a certificate from the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports. Again, 
sports equipment, imported by National Sports Federations or by individual 
sports persons can also get the benefit of custom duty exemption in the 
notified items. 
Sports Authority of India (SAI) also augments the efforts of the state 
government in promotion of sports at Junior, Sub-Junior and Senior Level. 
The SAI is implementing the following sports promotional scheme to identify 
talent in various sports disciplines in the age groups ranging from 8-25 years 
so as to excel at National & International Level. Under the following SAI's 
scheme sportspersons in 28 sports disciplines are admitted in SAI sports 
centers and provided with systematic  and scientific training to achieve 
excellence at various level of competition. 
(i) National Sports Talent Contest Scheme (NSTC) (8-14 years) 
(ii) Army Boys Sports Company (ABSC) (8-14 years) 
(iii) Special Area Games (SAG) (14-21 years) 
(iv) SAI Training Centre (STC) (14-21 years) (v)

Anti Doping Steps 
†1434. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will the Minister of YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) the measures being taken by Government to ensure that no Indian 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
 197 

RAJYA SABHA [15 December, 2004] 
sports person is found guilty of doping in international sports and put the 
country to shame; and 
(b) whether there is a proposal to  form an enquiry committee in the 
country also that can fi rmly present the case of innocent sports person at 
international level? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI SUNIL 
DUTT): (a) The Government of India has launched the Scheme for Dope Test 
in the 10th Five Year Plan with the objectives: (i) to have an International 
Olympic Committee-accredited Dope Control Centrel in India (ii) to maintain 
quality control system as required by International standard, i.e., ISO: 17025 
(iii) to educate athletes, coaches and other supporting personnel about the 
harmful effects of dope (iv) to test and develop the rationale for drug free 
sports and a national anti-doping policy (v) to conduct incompetition and out-
of-competition dope tests on sportspersons (vi) to promote research and 
training and (vii) to harmonize the dope-related regulations in tune with the 
World Anti Doping code and the rules and regulations framed by the World 
Anti Doping Agency from time to time. 
A Dope Control Centre (DCC) has been set up in Sports Authority of India 
located at JN Stadium, New Delhi which has already got ISO 9001:2000 
certification as well as ISO 17025:1999 certification. 
Government has dealt with the problem of doping in sports both at 
preventive and punitive levels. Elaborate efforts are being made by the Sports 
Authority of India to educate the pl ayers/sports-persons. National Sports 
Federations have been asked to take action against sportspersons found guilty 
of doping. Government of India has also taken disciplinary action against 
coaches in the light of positive dope result in respect of certain sports-persons 
coached by them. 
(b) No, Sir. However, cases of innoce nt sports-persons at International 
level are being presented by the con cerned National Sports Federation 
through Indian Olympic Association.

Need to connect hinterland in Kashmir by air service 
PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ (Jammu and Kashmir): Mr. Chairman, Sir, the 
far-flung areas in Kashmir have suffered severe neglect and deprivation for 
decades for want of essential services. The people of Gurez, Tulail, 
223 

RAJYA SABHA [15 December, 2004] 
Machil, Karnah and Keran remain cut off for months from Kashmir valley. In 
order to improve their living conditions , the first measure would be to make 
these areas accessible during winter months when the people suffer the most. 
When winter sets in and these areas get cut-off, the suffering sets in 
making people's life miserable. The system of communication is already non-
existent, or, dilapidated in these areas, and, once these places get cut-off, the 
otherwise fragile health-care system crumbles down completely and people 
suffer severe hardships. Many deaths are reported every year due to absence 
of transportation facilities for patients in critical condition, who can be saved if 
they are provided medical treatment in hospitals in Kashmir valley. 
The relief of all kinds will be available only when these areas become 
accessible. I, therefore, urge the Minist er for Civil Aviation to examine my 
proposal to provide air service to all the five places, namely, Gurez, Tulail, 
Machil, Karnah and Keran, and, connect these areas with Srinagar. It can be 
a helicopter service thrice a week, if not daily. A sing le air craft, say, a large 
helicopter is needed to connect these places with Srinagar. For a dynamic 
Minister of Civil Aviation, it should not be difficult to provide air-service in 
these areas in the near future. 
Need to formulate schemes to solve the problems of beggars in 
the country 
SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA TAIMUR (Assam): Hon. Chairman, Sir, I 
want to mention about t he problems of beggars in the country. Begging is a 
serious problem in our country. We should not only discourage people from 
becoming beggers, rather our objective should also be to provide gainful 
employment to all able-bodied men a nd women. However, there are people 
who are incapable of being gainfully em ployed, and, for this specific group 
who are in danger of becoming begger s, the society must lend a helping 
hand. 
After independence, the Government have made some plans for the 
development and also for the eradication  of poverty. The Panchayati Raj has 
also done much by implementing the schemes like 'Food for Work", DRDA, 
IRDP etc. But still there are hundreds of beggars in most of the 
224 

[15 December, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
States in India. Apart from handicapped and blind beggars, there are aged 
and ill-health beggars also. 
The Department of Social Welfare is providing oeggars' asylums in some 
of the States where training-cum-produc tion centres have also been setup. I 
think such asylums should also be made in those States where there are 
more beggars. The money allocated to help these specific groups should fully 
reach the target group. Further, some schemes should be made to help these 
beggars to become self-reliant. The main problem is that the money allocated 
under these schemes for these poor  and helpless people does not reach 
them fully. So, the Government should monitor it strictly. 
I, therefore, strongly urge upon the Government to formulate more 
schemes to mitigate the sufferings of homeless, aged and old beggars by 
making special plans to eradicate the beggars' menace in our country. 
Demand for removal of central excise duty exemption on unbranded 
beedies 
SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY SIRIGIREDDY (Andhra Pradesh): Mr. 
Chairman, Sir, I wish to bring to the notice of the Government of India the 
gross misuse of Central excise duty exemption given to the unbranded beedi 
manufactures in the country. Unbranded beedi manufacturers are exempted 
from excise duty, provided they manufacture less than 20,00,000 beedies per 
annum. The problem is, no customer pur chases unbranded beedies because 
literally there is no trade for unbranded beedies, since each trader has his 
own flavour which is represented by his brand. What the unscrupulous traders 
do is, they get beedies roiled, claim exemption and, by coercion, get 
counterfeit labels printed on popular brands and sell them in the market. 
Thereby, they are evading Centra! excise  duty and the benefits to be given to 
the labourers under the Beedi and Cigar Workers Act. The unscrupulous 
traders act cleverly by saying to the labourers that beedi labelling is a 
specialised skill and hence you will not be able to do it. Hence, exemption 
granted to small beedi manufacturer s becomes redundant. It is because the 
real beedi roller is not benefited fr om the exemption since duty is not 
collected. As a result, facilities extended through Labour Welfare Cess which, 
otherwise, is given to the statutory labourers, will not reach them.

recommended that exemption granted to  unbranded beedi manufacturers is 
counter-productive and should be remove d forthwith. Hence, I request the 
exemption granted to unbranded beed i manufacturers be withdrawn and 
printing of counterfeit beedi labels be made a congnisable offence.

Demand for harnessing the west-flowing river waters for use in the dry 
region of Tamil Nadu 
SHRI THANGATAMIL SELVAN (Tamil Nadu): Sir, I wish to bring to the 
notice of the Government the need to harness the surplus water of the west-
flowing rivers for use in the dry region of Tamil Nadu. In 1976, a committee 
was set up to look into the viability of  harnessing the water of west-flowing 
rivers. That committee found the scheme to be viable. The Planning 
Commission Report of 1978 also pointed out that 1,25,000 million cubic feet of 
water of 85 west-flowing rivers of Kerala  is running waste into the sea. So far, 
more than 20 rounds of talks have been held, yet, water continues to flow 
waste. The water resource of Tam il Nadu is just around 1350TMC. Of the 
2500 TMC water resources of Kerala, about 1100TMC water is flowing waste 
into the Arabian Sea. By harnessing the waste water and diverting it to Tamil 
Nadu, lakhs of acres in the rain-dep endent districts of Madurai, Theni, 
Thirunelveli, Tuticorin and Virudhunagar could be cultivated. Out of 180 TMC 
surplus water of Pambaiyaaru in Kerala, only 25 TMC water needs to be 
diverted. Diverting a part of the surplus water of Anaimalai, Idduki and Kallaru 
of Periyar delta will benefit Coimbatore and the Southern districts. Tamil Nadu 
has expressed its willingness to provide electricity, rice and cattle feed to 
Kerala in return . In view of the urgent requirement of water for Tamil Nadu 
from upper riparian States, I appeal to the Centre to intervene and take 
immediate steps to harness the west-flowing river water for use in Tamil Nadu.

project by a condition imposed by the Ministry of Environment and Forests

establishment. This condition is totally unrelated to the project, and there is no 
rationale in imposing it. The project when executed will benefit all citizens in 
Mumbai, including the large number of Naval personnel and their families who 
live in Mumbai, which is the headquar ters of the Western Naval Command.

been no positive response so far. In vi ew of the crucial importance of the 
project in decongesting the Western road network of Mumbai city, it is 
requested that urgent clearance may be  given to the project, withdrawing the 
condition imposed by the Ministry of Environment and Forests.

GOVERNMENT BILL 
The Special Tribunals (Supplementary Provisions) Repeal Bill, 
2004 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, 
PUBLIC GRIEVANCE SAND PENSIONS (SHRI SURESH PACHOURI): Sir, I 
beg to move: 
That the Bill to repeal the Special Tribunals (Supplementary Provisions) 
Act, 1946, as passed by Lok Sabha, be taken into consideration. 
Sir, the Special Tribunals (Supplementary Provisions) Act, 1946 was 
enacted to make certain provisions in relation to sentences and orders 
passed by Special Tribunals on such Tribunals ceasing to function. These 
Tribunals were earlier constituted under the Criminal Law amendment 
Ordinance, 1943 to provide for speedy trial and effective punishment for 
certain offences involving public serv ants, punishable under the Indian Penal 
Code. No Special Tribunal, so constitu ted, is in existence now. Moreover, 
orders and sentences passed by these Tribunals have already been acted 
upon. The special Tribunals (Supplementary Provisions) Repeal Act, 1946, 
has accordingly become obsolete. Further , the offences punishable by these 
Tribunals are now punishable under t he Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. 
Section 3 thereof empowers the Central and State Governments to appoint as 
many special judges as necessary to try offences punishable under the 
Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. 
The Commission on Review of Administrative Laws, constituted by the 
Central Government in May, 1988, has already recommended repeal of the 
Special Tribunals (Supplementary Provis ions) Act, 1946.1, therefore, request 
that the Bill may be taken into consideration by the House and be passed. 
The question was proposed. MR. 
DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Now, the question is: 
That the Bill to repeal the Special Tribunals (Supplementary Provisions) 
Act, 1946, as passed by Lok Sabha, be taken into consideration. 
The motion was adopted.

DR. P.C. ALEXANDER (MAHARASHTRA): Madam Vice-Chairman, I 
would like to begin with a few observations about our general attitude to 
internal security. As a nation, we have been attaching comparatively less 
importance to problems relevant to internal security than to external security. 
Somehow or the other, a philosophy seems to have developed among our 
people that once we have shaken off the foreign yoke and asserted our right 
to be our own masters in our own houses, sovereignty will automatically be 
preserved, security will automatically be part of the element of sovereignty; 
and, therefore, we are treating internal secu rity as if it is only a law and order 
problem. Confusing law and order with in ternal security has been the greatest 
weakness in our approach to internal security problems. That is my first point. 
277 

RAJYA SABHA [15 December, 2004] 
We are forgetting the lesson of post-World War-ll history. If we analyse 
what has happend to various nations in the post-world War period, we should 
really be much more concerned on the problem of internal security than what 
we are today. 
What happened to the Soviet Union? What happened to Yugoslavia? What 
has happensd to the numerous States in African conti nent? States have 
disappeared. States have got disintegra ted, States have failed, new States 
have emerged and the reason has not been an attack from outside, in most of 
these cases, In 90 per cent of the case s, where States have failed or fallen or 
got disintegrated, the real reason has been failure to maintain internal security. 
That lesson we have not yet understood properly. The second point I want to 
raise about internal security follows from the first. At the Central level, we think 
it is only the responsibility of the Home Mi nistry. At the State level, they think it 
is the responsibility only of the Home Department. Internal security, Madam, 
Vice-Chairperson, is not merely a matter for the Home Ministry or the Home 
Minister. The Education Ministry for ex ample, in my opinion, has an equal 
reponsibility to ensure internal security because it is only by educating the 
youth of the country, the young children of the country, on the spirit of true 
patriotism, on the param ount need of love of one's own country, on the 
importance of national integration, that we can maintain security. If we know 
the history of the united States in the early stages of its formation and how will 
they used schools and syllabi to promote national integration and to build up 
one nation out of a multitude of the nationals of the world who had chosen to 
be emigrants to that country, we can lear n a lesson from that. But we do not 
consider education as a tool for natio nal integration or and for maintaining 
internal security. I do not agree with the comments made either by General 
Shankar Roy Choudhry or by Shri Ashwani Kumar that this is a matter for the 
State Governments and therefore we should interfere with the least. I will 
come to that when I deal with Naxalite problem which is the main subject of my
